summary: Elevated TTFB on chat completions after runtime/model upgrade
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports elevated time-to-first-token (TTFB) for chat completion endpoints immediately after we rolled out runtime v2.14 and model redwood-rlhf-v2-7B to their dedicated pool. The delay is observed from the first token (slow response start) even for short prompts.

Impact:
- StreamAI reports 30-60s TTFB on ~20% of requests to /v1/chat/completions.
- Requests eventually complete (no 5xx), but perceived latency is causing user-facing timeouts in their front-end.
- Affected customer is on Dedicated capacity with an SLA; business impact: degraded user experience and support escalation.

Environment:
- Customer: StreamAI Inc.
- Tier: dedicated
- Region: us-east primary, affects some cross-region routing to us-west
- Runtime: serving-runtime v2.14 (rolled out 2026-02-25 03:10 UTC)
- Models: redwood-rlhf-v2-7B (pinned), fallback redwood-rlhf-v2-13B observed in routing logs

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Send a minimal chat completion request to /v1/chat/completions with stream=false and short prompt ("Hello")
2) Observe TTFB ~30s for ~1/5 of requests; subsequent tokens stream normally after first token is returned
3) Reverting to runtime v2.13 removes the elevated TTFB in their environment

Logs / Evidence:
- Customer provided request IDs: req_20260225_8241, req_20260225_8253 (attached in ticket)
- Gateway traces show upstream latency concentrated in serving-runtime pre-token stage (controller -> worker handshake + kvcache lookup)
- Metrics: 95th percentile TTFB for their pool jumped from 120ms to 8.1s post-deploy; 99th from 450ms to 28s
- Autoscaler events show brief node churn during rollout window but no sustained OOMs

Initial hypothesis:
- A change in runtime v2.14 altered cold-start or KV cache warmup behavior for pinned models, causing high first-token latency when cache misses occur or worker handshakes stall under certain threading conditions.
- Potential mis-selection of quantized kernel path for 7B variant leading to serialization/initialization stalls.

Workaround applied so far:
- Rolled back the customer's Dedicated pool to runtime v2.13 (mitigation applied 2026-02-25 09:40 UTC). Customer reports latency returned to baseline after rollback.

Requested next steps:
- Investigation by SRE/Runtime team to root cause and determine whether this regression could affect other dedicated customers or hosted pools.
- Postmortem and rollback criteria added to runbook if rollout path needs to be changed.

investigation_notes: Reproduced in staging with stress scenario that simulates high prefix variance; TTFB spike occurs when worker receives first request after short idle and kv-cache miss triggers initialization path.

Profiling shows a 10-30s blocking call inside kernel probe helper introduced in v2.14 when certain quantized kernels are probed on specific GPU drivers (NVIDIA driver 540.x) under particular CPU thread scheduling.
Autoscaler churn correlated but not causal; node allocation delays amplify symptom but rollback eliminated issue without scale-down changes.
Related PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4521 (reverts kernel probe order).
Suggested mitigation: revert change in v2.14 or gate the probe change behind a feature flag for dedicated pools until validated across driver matrix.
Flagging for release manager: ensure coordinated communication to Dedicated customers with pinned models before next runtime rollout.
current_actions: Runtime team preparing hotfix release v2.14.1 that reverts kernel probe ordering and adds extra probes tests. SRE to schedule customer patch window and re-verify TTFB on StreamAI's pool. Support to notify customer of planned patch with ETA.
